payload.rationale: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 6.95% on September 17, 2026, having risen 19 basis points from the previous week and 30 basis points over the past month. To resolve YES, the rate on September 24 must exceed 7.01%, requiring a further increase of at least 7 basis points. While weekly changes of this magnitude are common, requiring a specific directional move of this size from the current level makes it less than a coin flip. Strongest reason the estimate could be too high: The recent 19 basis point jump may have overshot, leading to a stabilization or slight mean reversion in the upcoming week. Strongest reason the estimate could be too low: The strong upward momentum over the last month could easily persist, and a 7 basis point increase is well within normal weekly volatility.
limitations: Only five weeks of historical data provided.
No current data on 10-year Treasury yields or other leading indicators for the days between September 17 and September 19.
